allowedWork: Minimal Lisp semantics, exact evaluator fixture, canonical asset, runtime frames, native settled renderer, and Lisp-local botanical presentation.
One internal botanical Lisp catalogue asset and one internal tutorial route at /tutorials/programming/lisp-function-application/.
Reuse existing tutorial URL, TOC, scrubber, review, runtime, catalogue, and Svelte host boundaries.
After the local Lisp tutorial passes, compare economics, Lisp, and KpLessonDocument and extract only lifecycle-identical lesson mechanics.
Migrate economics and Lisp to caller-proven shared document, motion, navigation, control, token, and replaceable Svelte lesson-shell seams.
Add stable scoped unit, browser, visual, accessibility, performance, architecture, and release evidence.
Delete only local mechanics made obsolete by the verified two-caller migration.
disallowedWork: Do not implement a general Lisp parser, VM, meta-circular evaluator, quote, closures, continuations, macros, arbitrary execution, or other languages.
Do not promote botanical motifs or create a generic programming-language pack, universal scene graph, stage grammar, motif registry, or animation schema.
Do not implement generated solve-x, SvelteKit, Internal Studio, Public Web, mission site, Public Editor, or catalogue-wide lesson rollout.
Do not move domain semantics, clocks, renderer truth, stage choreography, or salience profiles into Svelte or shared lesson code.
Do not change economics semantics, approved visuals, URLs, performance ceilings, or the stable animation-promotion ledger.
Do not add client KaTeX, client syntax-highlighter bundles, live LLM prose, or runtime editorial calls.

Stop on identity inferred from glyph equality, invented evaluator semantics, loss of native settled code, nondeterministic seek/rewind, provenance gaps, scroll jumps, multiple samplers, economics regression, domain branches in shared code, wider budgets, unrelated-file overlap, missing proof, or the final human checkpoint.
goal: Build an exact botanical Lisp function-application asset and tutorial, then extract only lesson mechanics proven by both Lisp and the approved economics tutorial while preserving framework-neutral semantic and renderer authority.

slices.title: Activate contract and freeze baselines
slices.summary: Activated the human-approved 28-slice contract, aligned roadmap and supporting threads, froze the economics preservation baseline and Lisp acceptance boundary, and kept the matrix promotion ledger unchanged. Promotion-memory, workspace validation, and patch hygiene pass.

slices.title: Define minimal Lisp semantic model
slices.summary: Added a deeply immutable, validator-backed Lisp semantic model for atoms, lists, source spans, distinct binder/reference occurrences, lexical bindings, environments, typed substitution destinations, and exact integer values. Four focused tests and the full repository typecheck pass; no parser, evaluator, renderer, or framework dependency was introduced.

slices.title: Add exact lambda evaluator fixture
slices.summary: Added the exact ((lambda (x) (+ x 1)) 4) fixture and a deliberately bounded evaluator that certifies x-to-4 binding, destination provenance, (+ 4 1) reconstruction, and exact result 5 independently of animation. Eight focused tests and app/test TypeScript checks pass.

slices.title: Compile canonical Lisp animation asset
slices.summary: Compiled the certified Lisp fixture into canonical KP asset objects, selectors, strict semantic transformations, reversible correspondence maps, substitution/evaluation lineage graphs, four checkpoints, accessibility truth, and an explicit five-entry material ledger. Twelve tests and app/test TypeScript checks pass.

slices.title: Project deterministic Lisp runtime frames
slices.summary: Added a pure deterministic Lisp runtime-frame sampler with five semantic stages, exact checkpoint focus, native expression payloads, accessible descriptions, and explicit per-entry material conservation. Dense seek and rewind tests plus app/test TypeScript checks pass.

slices.title: Render native settled S-expressions
slices.summary: Added a framework-neutral Lisp HTML renderer whose application, environment, reconstructed form, and result settle as selectable native code. Transient motion has a distinct aria-hidden layer, every frame exposes equivalent live text, and nine focused tests plus app/test TypeScript checks pass.

slices.title: Plan local botanical presentation
slices.summary: Added one experimental Lisp-local botanical presentation plan with enclosure, branch, leaf, root, bud, and fruit roles bound to exact semantic selectors. Three semantic paths account for all five material-ledger entries; native code and checkpoint crossfades remain authoritative. Seven focused tests and app/test TypeScript checks pass.

slices.title: Render reversible botanical animation
slices.summary: Rendered the local botanical plan as one framework-neutral stage with flexible enclosure, branches, binding root, leaf, buds, fruit, and three material paths. Absolute progress gives exact seek/rewind, reduced motion snaps to checkpoints, and native code plus nonvisual truth remain authoritative. Eleven focused tests and app/test TypeScript checks pass.

slices.title: Register catalogue asset and visual harness
slices.summary: Wrapped the Lisp fixture as a valid programming animation asset, registered it in eager/lazy catalogues and generated editor metadata, retained experimental-local status, and added stable visual:botanical-lisp-asset capture with five frames. The capture exposed and repaired native-stage overprint. Ten catalogue/projection tests, full typecheck, metadata freshness, promotion-memory, and visual capture pass.

slices.title: Author canonical Lisp lesson prose
slices.summary: Authored the canonical continuous Lisp lesson around provenance: four compact h3 sections, about 1,100 words, and two prose-surrounded motion boundaries for binding/reconstruction and evaluation/gathering. The text distinguishes occurrences, substitution, and evaluation, limits the botanical metaphor, and keeps native code authoritative. Three editorial tests pass.

slices.title: Compile local Lisp publication payload
slices.summary: Added a narrow local Markdown compiler and publication projection with escaped continuous prose, native inline code, four semantic section destinations, ordered passage/motion blocks, static TOC links, and two final-geometry text-free scrubbers. Six focused tests and app/test TypeScript checks pass; no client parser or syntax highlighter was added.

slices.title: Host local Svelte tutorial route
slices.summary: Mounted /tutorials/programming/lisp-function-application/ through a thin lazy Svelte shell with h3 headings, continuous indented prose, fixed left TOC, persistent contiguous right stage, static motion controls, and Review capture. Semantic models, samplers, renderer, URLs, and controls remain framework-neutral. Ten focused tests, zero Svelte diagnostics, app/test TypeScript, and production build pass; the route emits separate 8.75 kB JS and 1.26 kB CSS gzip chunks.

slices.title: Bind application and substitution motion block
slices.summary: Bound the first prose scrubber to global progress 0 through 0.74 using one local controller over the canonical playback reducer and Lisp sampler. Seek, checkpoints, play, pause, and rewind stop exactly at reconstructed (+ 4 1); Svelte remains a static composition host. Split scrubber event names into a DOM-neutral contract after a focused Node portability failure. Eleven focused tests, Svelte diagnostics, and app/test TypeScript pass.

slices.title: Bind cumulative evaluation motion block
slices.summary: Bound both prose scrubbers to one canonical playback session and sampler. The first maps global progress 0–0.74, the second 0.74–1, their exact boundary is shared, and earlier controls remain cumulatively complete while later motion plays. Fourteen focused tests, Svelte diagnostics, app/test TypeScript, and patch hygiene pass.

slices.title: Add Lisp salience projection
slices.summary: Added a Lisp-local salience projection derived from canonical runtime selectors. It marks stage target/context/attenuated nodes and material paths, applies stable before/after passage treatment without mutating prose, and preserves native code. Fourteen focused tests, five representative captures, Svelte diagnostics, app/test TypeScript, and patch hygiene pass.

slices.title: Restore semantic deep links transactionally
slices.summary: Added a local destination registry and navigation controller that maps every section, block, and named checkpoint directly to one cumulative semantic state. Direct loads, visible nested TOC jumps, and Back/Forward restore motion before scrolling with one progress write and no progress in the URL. Unit/navigation tests, focused Chromium, full typecheck, and patch hygiene pass after correcting lesson-root ownership exposed by the initial browser run.

slices.title: Coordinate scroll and manual ownership
slices.summary: Added Lisp-local authored scroll corridors with semantic holds, 38% reading-band cues, one active block, wheel/touch/keyboard intent, manual and navigation takeover, continuous rebasing, and exact reverse sampling through the canonical motion controller. Twelve focused tests, four Chromium interactions, full typecheck, and patch hygiene pass after correcting smooth-scroll test geometry and subpixel hold settlement.

slices.title: Complete responsive and accessible projections
slices.summary: Completed phone containment, reduced-motion manual semantics, system high-contrast emphasis, one-current-form screen-reader state, and compiler-owned static/no-JS publication markup. Fifteen cross-browser accessibility checks, nine combined Chromium interactions, twelve focused tests, full typecheck, and patch hygiene pass after moving forced-color rules to the renderer-owned late stylesheet.

slices.title: Certify local tutorial visuals and performance
slices.summary: Added stable test:botanical-lisp-tutorial, visual:botanical-lisp-tutorial, and performance:botanical-lisp-tutorial commands with committed visual and production probes. Fifty-eight local tests pass; six visual states pass containment review after centering native code and waiting for scroll settlement; production uses 96.2kB transfer/77.4kB script/24 resources with zero initial CLS, 34.4ms active p95, no active long tasks, and no KaTeX/Monaco/Three route resources. Architecture and promotion-memory checks pass; botanical remains experimental-local.

slices.title: Compare economics Lisp and lesson document seams
slices.summary: Committed a typed seam ledger and field-by-field KpLessonDocument comparison. It proves two-caller extraction candidates for slices 21-25, reuses existing URL/TOC/scrubber primitives, and keeps inline rendering, stage semantics, focus geometry, and domain runtimes local. Five ledger tests, full typecheck, architecture gates, and patch hygiene pass.

slices.title: Reconcile shared lesson publication document
slices.summary: Added a framework-neutral tutorial publication wrapper whose content authority is the existing validated KpLessonDocument. Economics and Lisp adapters preserve raw source syntax, h3 headings, typed asset refs, checkpoints converted to permille, and optional tutorial metadata while local KaTeX/code HTML remains an adapter projection. Thirty focused caller/reader tests, full typecheck, architecture gates, and patch hygiene pass.

slices.title: Extract shared motion and scroll mechanics
slices.summary: Extracted framework- and domain-neutral motion types, cumulative block projection, dense corridor/inverse/rebase math, reading-band ownership, and one-rAF scroll coordinator. Economics wrappers and Lisp controller now use the shared mechanics while keeping semantic scene/frame paint local. Economics 24 tests, Lisp 58 tests, 26 focused shared/caller tests, 14 Chromium interactions, full typecheck, architecture gates, and patch hygiene pass.

slices.title: Extract shared navigation transactions
slices.summary: Extracted a framework-neutral semantic navigation controller used by both tutorials. It owns TOC intent, semantic history, duplicate popstate/hash suppression, listener lifecycle, and restore-before-active-before-scroll ordering while caller callbacks retain reconstruction and geometry. Twenty-four focused tests, 14 Chromium navigation/interaction tests, full typecheck, architecture gates, and patch hygiene pass.

slices.title: Extract shared static publication controls
slices.summary: Added one shared static publication-control compiler over KpLessonDocument, existing TOC/scrubber renderers, and semantic URLs. Economics and Lisp now supply only route and block labels; final light DOM, fallback links, disabled pre-upgrade controls, and checkpoint geometry remain shared. Twenty-two focused tests, 17 Chromium no-JS/accessibility/interaction tests, full typecheck, architecture gates, and patch hygiene pass.

slices.title: Extract shared lesson shell and tokens
slices.summary: Extracted a replaceable shared Svelte lesson shell and domain-adaptable CSS tokens, then composed both economics and Lisp hosts through it without moving semantic paint or focus policy. Shared styles fold into each route stylesheet; lazy tutorial seams, route probes, and dependency-free catalog identities are consolidated without eager-loading implementations. Twenty-six focused tests, 14 current visual checks, both production performance probes, architecture, type/build checks, and patch hygiene pass. Economics remains at its unchanged 48-resource ceiling with 310.4kB transfer, 236.8kB script, 122ms startup task, and 36ms active p95.

slices.title: Migrate economics and prune superseded mechanics
slices.summary: Migrated the approved economics exemplar directly onto the shared lesson motion, navigation, document, controls, tokens, and shell seams. Deleted the superseded corridor/coordinator pass-through modules and obsolete economics TOC builder, added a durable shared-seam conformance gate, and retained checkpoints, graph composition, verification, salience, and parameters as domain-local projections. Twenty-six economics tests, 12 browser/visual checks, production build/typecheck, architecture, and patch hygiene pass; the preserved 48-resource budget, exact URLs, no-JS controls, phone layout, and 33.5ms active p95 remain intact.

slices.title: Migrate Lisp and prove shared conformance
slices.summary: Migrated Lisp fully onto the shared document, motion, navigation, controls, tokens, and replaceable shell seams. Removed local corridor/frame/rebase wrapper exports, aligned the no-JS static projection with shared shell classes, strengthened the one-path two-caller contract suite, added Lisp conformance gates, and documented the explicitly experimental botanical APIs. Sixty Lisp tests, 17 shared/gold conformance tests, 16 combined route interactions, 15 cross-browser accessibility checks, catalogue and tutorial visuals, production build/performance, architecture, promotion memory, and patch hygiene pass. Production Lisp uses 101.5kB transfer, 81.9kB script, 21 resources, zero initial CLS, and 33.7ms active p95.
